newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Alfa seen earning good results.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Alfa seen earning good results.

text.p: MEXICO CITY, April 11 (Ruter) - Alfa S.A. is expected to show continued good performance on an operating basis for most of its group in the first quarter of the year, analysts said.
But they added the company will see fewer benefits than before from monetary gains, which derive from accounting rules aimed at compensating for inflation.

The Monterrey-based conglomerate is expected to show per share earnings of between 1.68 pesos per share and 1.83 pesos per share, two analysts said. A third analyst forecast 1.053 pesos per share, while acknowledging the estimate was much lower than the most.
Alfa, one of Mexico's biggest companies, has five divisions made up of steel (Hylsamex), petrochemicals (Alpek), food (Sigma), telecommunications (Onexa) and retail and auto parts (Versax).
"You are going to find that on an operating basis, the results will be better, but the bottom line will not benefit so much from monetary gains," said Bear, Stearns analyst Santiago Pique.
Analysts said that where the company could be hurt is in its Alpek subsidiary, which faces depressed worldwide chemical prices.
D.A. Campbell analyst Gus M. Araya said certain components of Alfa will show good growth, particulary Sigma. Hylsamex is also seen posting stronger domestic sales, he said.
Valores Finamex brokerage said in a report that estimated net income is 1.0 billion pesos, down 42 percent, or earnings of 1.68 pesos per share.

"Neither pricing nor the peso have been favorable for Alfa during the first quarter 1997. Both Hylsa and especially Alpek will report significantly lower average sales prices in pesos," said Valores Finamex analyst Angeli Hemm in a report.

"Though sales volumes for all divisions is expected to increase, lower peso pricing will cause consolidated sales to fall an estimated 11.5 percent. Exports in dollars should decline to $215 million from $272 million," she added.
Valores said that a year ago the operating margin was 17.2 percent, but is expected to fall to 15.76 percent.
Alfa's operating income is expected to decline 18.7 percent to 1.09 billion pesos, she said.
EBITDA is seen rising to $190.7 million in first quarter 1997, compared to $186.2 million in first quarter 1996, Valores said.
Alfa had per share earnings of 6.55 pesos in 1996. Revenues were 27.83 billion pesos in 1996 compared with 27.49 billion in 1995.
Net profit was 3.928 billion pesos in 1996 compared with 2.218 billion pesos in 1995.
